content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Jason Hansen (E044) requests admin access to Payroll.

The notes: 5 notes say he's a full-time Engineer. 1 note (Security) says he's a contractor with basic security training.

Access policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if the employee's role owns the system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

Payroll is owned by Payroll Specialist role.

Jason is an Engineer (per most notes). Engineers don't own Payroll.

If full-time: max is write (since Engineer doesn't own Payroll, admin not allowed). Requested admin > write, so grant write.

If contractor with basic training: max is read. Requested admin > read, so grant read.

There's a conflict between notes: most say full-time Engineer, security says contractor with basic training. Hmm.

Which to trust? The security DB is specifically about employment type perhaps. But 5 other notes from HR, IT, Finance, Compliance, Facilities all say full-time Engineer. The Security note says contractor.

As the Approver, I need to make a decision. The majority of evidence suggests full-time Engineer, which caps at write. The security note suggests contractor with basic training, which caps at read.

Hmm, conflicting facts. This is a tricky one. The task says "Use the information available to you to make your decision."

Given the conflicting evidence, most notes (5 of 6) confirm full-time Engineer. The security note is the outlier. I'll go with the majority: full-time Engineer => max write. Requested admin > write, so grant write.

Let me submit decision: write.
